label: Usurp title command
summary: The command behind the title window's usurp button, which takes the shown title from its holder.
details: The title window (the panel that opens when you click a title) checks it with IsValidCommand to enable the usurp button and passes it to CreateCommandPopup on click. Going by its name, the player gets a confirmation popup; the game documents nothing more.

label: Usurp button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the title window's usurp button.
details: Vanilla shows it on the usurp button, next to the usurp command. Going by its name, it explains whether and why the title can be usurped; the game documents nothing more.

label: De jure vassal groups
summary: The groups of titles listed under the shown title in the title window.
details: Vanilla fills a list with it; each item (DeJureVassalGroupItem) holds title entries and an "owned by" text. When it is empty, the window shows that the title has no de jure (rightful, by law) titles below it. Going by these uses; the game documents nothing more.

label: Go to holding
summary: Opens the holding view of the shown title when its button is clicked.
details: Vanilla puts it on a button in the title window that shows the holding's province name; the button's tooltip reads "Click to go to holding view".

label: Has enough counties
summary: Whether the player holds enough of the title's counties to create it.
details: Vanilla shows a check mark when true and a cross when false, next to the minimum de jure (rightful territory) requirement in the title creation part of the title window. Going by these uses; the game documents nothing more.

label: Has enough gold
summary: Whether the player has enough gold to create the shown title.
details: Vanilla shows a check mark or a cross next to the minimum gold requirement; that row is hidden for governments that pay piety instead of gold for new titles. Going by these uses; the game documents nothing more.

label: Has enough piety level
summary: Whether the player's piety level is high enough to create the shown title.
details: Vanilla uses it in a text that puts a check or a cross before "Requires" and the needed piety level. Going by its name and this use; the game documents nothing more.

label: Has merit pool data
summary: Whether the title window has a merit pool description to show for the title.
details: Vanilla shows the merit pool description text only when it is true. What a merit pool is in detail the input does not say; the game documents nothing more.

label: Has titles of tier
summary: Whether the player meets the title creation requirement about already holding titles of a certain rank.
details: Vanilla shows a check mark or a cross with the "titles of tier" requirement text when creating a title. The row is shown only when the requirement is not met and the government pays gold, not piety, for new titles. Going by these uses; the game documents nothing more.

label: Player in clerical region
summary: Whether the player is in the clerical region of the shown title.
details: Vanilla uses it, for titles with a clerical region, to show a "my clerical region" label when the player is in it or holds the title. Going by its name and this one use; the game documents nothing more.

label: Title is barony
summary: Going by its name, whether the title shown in the title window is a barony.
details: Vanilla never uses it; the window checks Title.IsBarony instead. The game documents nothing more.

label: Title is county
summary: Going by its name, whether the title shown in the title window is a county.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Make primary title
summary: Makes the shown title the player's primary title when its button is clicked.
details: Vanilla puts it on the "make primary" button, shown only on the player's own titles when CanMakePrimary allows it and the player's variable hide_make_primary_title is not above 0. Going by its name and this use.

label: Open claimants
summary: Going by its name, opens the list of characters with a claim on the shown title.
details: Vanilla never uses it; its claimants button uses ToggleClaimants. The game documents nothing more.

label: Open election
summary: Opens the election window for the shown title.
details: Vanilla puts it on the round "View Election" button, shown for titles with elective succession that have no clerical region.

label: Title window itself
summary: A function on the title window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types (for example Character.Self passed as an argument); those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Shows appointment
summary: Whether the title window shows appointment of the successor instead of the plain line of succession.
details: When true, vanilla shows the successor candidate list (with scores and ways to invest in a candidate); when false, it shows the line of succession portraits. Going by these uses; the game documents nothing more.

label: Shows destroy button
summary: Whether the title window shows the button to destroy the shown title.
details: Vanilla also hides the button for clerical regions and titles with a clerical elector. Whether the destruction is allowed is checked separately by the destroy command.

label: Shows usurp button
summary: Whether the title window shows the button to usurp the shown title.
details: Vanilla shows the button only when the title's holder is not the player, and for nomad players only for titles not above their primary title's rank. Whether the usurpation is allowed is checked separately by the usurp command.

label: Toggle claimants
summary: Opens or closes the list of claimants of the shown title.
details: Vanilla puts it on the "Claimants" button, which is enabled only when the title has at least one claimant (a character with a claim on it).

label: Toggle find vassal
summary: Opens or closes the "find vassal" list, for picking a character to hand the shown title to.
details: Vanilla shows the button only on the player's own titles that allow it and are not leased out. Going by its name, the button's art (granting a title to a vassal) and these conditions.

label: Toggle title history
summary: Opens or closes the history of the shown title.
details: Vanilla puts it on the "show title history" button, which is hidden for baronies and titles that have a faction.

label: Toggle laws
summary: Opens or closes the panel for adding laws to the shown title.
details: Vanilla puts it on the "add laws" button, shown only on the player's own titles when CanAddLaws allows it.

label: Access toast handler
summary: A function on the toast handler (the pop-up notifications) that, going by its name, hands back the handler itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Dismiss all toasts
summary: Closes all toast messages (short pop-up notifications) at once.
details: Vanilla binds it to right-clicking a dismiss button of the toasts; a plain click on that button runs DismissMessage, and its tooltip points to the right click for dismissing all.

label: Dismiss toast
summary: Closes the current toast message (a short pop-up notification).
details: Vanilla binds it to right-clicking the toast and to clicking its dismiss buttons.

label: Toast message
summary: The message a toast (a short pop-up notification) shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the toast templates, so the parts inside read their texts from it. The game documents no return type.

label: Has toast
summary: Whether there is a toast message to show.
details: Vanilla shows the toast only when this is true, the barbershop (appearance editor) is closed and no paused succession is showing in single player.

label: Toast handler itself
summary: A function on the toast handler that, going by its name, hands back the handler itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Hold toast
summary: Called when the mouse enters a toast; going by its name, it holds the toast so it does not close meanwhile.
details: Vanilla calls it when the mouse enters the toast and StopDelayingMessage when it leaves. The game documents nothing more.

label: Release toast
summary: Called when the mouse leaves a toast; going by its name, it lets the toast run out again.
details: The counterpart of StartDelayingMessage, which vanilla calls when the mouse enters the toast. The game documents nothing more.

label: Access parameter
summary: A function on a token parameter that, going by its name, hands back the parameter itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Parameter yes/no value
summary: Going by its name, the value of a token parameter read as yes or no.
details: Vanilla never uses it. A token parameter is probably a named setting such as a doctrine parameter (see GetIntValue); the game documents nothing more.

label: Parameter decimal value
summary: Going by its name, the value of a token parameter as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Parameter whole number
summary: The value of a parameter as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it in the descriptions of doctrine parameters (settings that tenets and doctrines carry), where the number is turned into a hostility level name, as in "Considers other faiths that share their head of faith to be (hostility level)".

label: Parameter itself
summary: A function on a token parameter that, going by its name, hands back the parameter itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Dialog buttons

details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents no return type and nothing more.

label: Close dialog

details: Vanilla's GUI animation editor runs it right after a track is added from its new track dialog, so going by that use the dialog closes once a choice is made. It is part of the engine's tools, not of the game itself.

label: Close dialog

details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines with "Close" are ordinary texts, not uses. The game documents nothing more.

label: Confirm dialog
summary: Going by its name, confirms a tool dialog (part of the engine's internal tools).
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; EndPrepConfirm.Confirm in the multiplayer screen is a different type and only a hint. The game documents nothing more.

label: Tool dialog itself
summary: A function on a tool dialog that, going by its name, hands back the dialog itself.
details: Part of the engine's internal GUI. Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Dialog title

details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines with "Title" are about game titles, not this. The game documents nothing more.

label: Access dialog button
summary: A function on a button of a tool dialog that, going by its name, hands back the button itself.
details: Part of the engine's internal GUI. Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

details: Part of the engine's internal GUI. Vanilla never names it on this type; OnClick after other types (war items, schemes in the bottom bar) is only a hint. What the yes or no means the game does not document.

label: Dialog button itself

details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Dialog button text
summary: Going by its name, the text on a tool dialog's button.
details: Part of the engine's internal GUI. Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Access message dialog

details: Part of the engine's internal GUI. Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Is error message

details: Part of the engine's internal GUI, next to IsWarning and IsInfo. Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Is info message
summary: Going by its name, whether a tool message dialog only gives information.
details: Part of the engine's internal GUI, next to IsError and IsWarning. Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Is warning message
summary: Going by its name, whether a tool message dialog gives a warning.
details: Part of the engine's internal GUI, next to IsError and IsInfo. Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Dialog message
summary: Going by its name, the message text of a tool message dialog.
details: Part of the engine's internal GUI. Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Message dialog itself

details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Property color

details: It returns a color with four parts (red, green, blue, opacity). Vanilla never names it on this type; GetColor after other types is only a hint.

label: Property label
summary: The label text of a tool property (an editable setting in the engine's internal tools).
details: The map editor's smart material brush shows it as the heading of the frame that holds a property, such as its opacity curve.

label: Property tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a tool property (an editable setting in the engine's internal tools).
details: The GUI animation editor shows it when the mouse is over a property's row.

label: Property is active
summary: Going by its name, whether a tool property (an editable setting in the engine's internal tools) is active.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; IsActive after other types (holy sites, council tasks) is only a hint. What "active" means here the game does not document.

label: Tool property itself
summary: A function on a tool property that, going by its name, hands back the property itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access yes/no property

details: Part of the engine's internal tools. Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Property is on
summary: Going by its name, whether a yes/no tool property is switched on.
details: Part of the engine's internal tools; SetEnabled changes it. Vanilla never names it on this type; IsEnabled after other types (the music player) is only a hint.

label: Yes/no property itself
summary: A function on a yes/no tool property that, going by its name, hands back the property itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Switch property

details: Part of the engine's internal tools; IsEnabled reads the value. Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Access color property

details: Part of the engine's internal tools. Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Property color value
summary: Going by its name, the color stored in a color tool property.
details: It returns a color with four parts (red, green, blue, opacity). Part of the engine's internal tools; SetCColor changes it. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Color property itself
summary: A function on a color tool property that, going by its name, hands back the property itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Set property color
summary: Going by its name, changes the color stored in a color tool property.
details: Part of the engine's internal tools; GetCColor reads it. Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Access text property
summary: A function on a text tool property that, going by its name, hands back the property itself.
details: Part of the engine's internal tools. Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Property text
summary: The text stored in a text tool property of the engine's internal tools.
details: The GUI animation editor shows it in the property's text box; SetString saves what is typed there.

label: Text property itself
summary: A function on a text tool property that, going by its name, hands back the property itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Save property text
summary: Saves the text typed into the box of a text tool property; it returns nothing.
details: The GUI animation editor runs it when editing of the box ends with a change. It takes no value: the text comes from the box itself. GetString reads the stored text.

label: Access color setting
summary: A function on a color tool property (a second color kind beside ToolPropertyCColor) that, going by its name, hands back the property itself.
details: Part of the engine's internal tools. Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Color setting value
summary: Going by its name, the color stored in this color tool property.
details: It returns a color with four parts (red, green, blue, opacity); SetColor changes it. Vanilla never names it on this type; GetColor after other types is only a hint.

label: Color setting itself
summary: A function on this color tool property that, going by its name, hands back the property itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Set color setting
summary: Going by its name, changes the color stored in this color tool property.
details: Part of the engine's internal tools; GetColor reads it. Vanilla never names it on this type; the culture windows' SetColor belongs to other types and is only a hint.

label: Access curve property
summary: A function on a curve tool property that, going by its name, hands back the property itself.
details: Part of the engine's internal tools. Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Curve preview
summary: A small preview picture of the curve stored in a curve tool property.
details: It takes four values: the picture's width and height in pixels and two colors in ARGB form (alpha, red, green, blue as hex). The map editor's smart material brush writes `( '(int32)400', '(int32)80', '(hex)66272A33', '(hex)FFA1A1A1' )` and shows the picture at half that size for sharper lines. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Width of the picture in pixels.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Height of the picture in pixels.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The first color (vanilla's comment calls it color A).

label: Curve editor open
summary: Whether a curve tool property has its curve editor open (yes or no), going by its name.
details: The smart material brush's curve editor button uses the opposite of it as its pressed state, next to ToggleCurveEditor, which opens or closes the editor. Why the button shows pressed while the editor is closed is not explained.

label: Open curve editor
summary: Going by its name, opens the editor for the curve of a curve tool property.
details: Part of the engine's internal tools. Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Reset curve
summary: Puts the curve of a curve tool property back to its default shape; it returns nothing.
details: The map editor's smart material brush runs it from a button whose tooltip says it resets the curve to default.

label: Curve property itself
summary: The curve tool property itself, to hand to another function.
details: The smart material brush passes it to CopyCurveToClipboard, so its Copy button copies this property's curve to the brush's own clipboard. The game documents no return type.

label: Set curve
summary: Replaces the curve stored in a curve tool property with the given one; it returns nothing.
details: It takes one value: the new curve. The smart material brush's Paste button runs it with the curve from the brush's clipboard (`GetCurveFromClipboard`).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a curve, such as the one on the brush's clipboard

label: Toggle curve editor
summary: Opens or closes the curve editor of a curve tool property; it returns nothing.
details: The map editor's smart material brush runs it from a button whose tooltip says it opens or closes the curve editor.

label: Access decimal property

details: Part of the engine's internal tools. Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.
